column1: # Differences between kyo-email's model and one built from Apache James mime4j 0.8.15's DOM by the same classification rules,
# over the vendored CPython, Stalwart, mime4j and Thunderbird messages. Kept by hand:
# EmailMessageReferenceTest prints, in this format, each row missing here and each row here that no longer occurs.
# Columns, tab-separated: message, aspect, the module's value, the reference's value, reason.
# Backslash, tab, CR and LF in a value are written as \\, \t, \r and \n, and any other control character as \uXXXX.
# Reasons, each the first rule of EmailMessageReference.classify that holds:

#   EncapsulatedMessageRewritten: a message/rfc822 part: mime4j parses it and the reference takes the message DefaultMessageWriter writes back, which is not the octets as they arrived; the module keeps those octets

#   CommentAsDisplayName: an address with no display name is followed by a comment, which the module takes as the name (the RFC 822 form, RFC 5322 appendix A.1.2's reading of it); mime4j drops comments
#   DuplicateAddressFields: the message has more than one To or Cc field; the module concatenates them as RFC 5322 section 4.5.3 says, mime4j takes the first
#   ObsoleteZoneName: the date's zone is one of the eight North American names, which RFC 5322 section 4.3 gives offsets; the module applies them, mime4j reads them as UTC
#   BoundaryTrailingWhiteSpace: a boundary parameter ends in white space, which the module removes before matching (RFC 2046 section 5.1.1), so lines mime4j reads as text are delimiters
#   Rfc2231ContentType: a Content-Type field holds a parameter in RFC 2231's form (name*=), the boundary or charset among them; the module reads it, mime4j does not

#   BoundaryReused: two nested multiparts declare the same boundary, which RFC 2046 section 5.1 forbids a composer; the innermost open one owns its delimiters in the module, mime4j splits them otherwise

#   OuterDelimiterInsidePart: a part of an inner multipart holds a line starting with an enclosing multipart's delimiter, which RFC 2046 section 5.1 forbids a composer; the module ends the inner multiparts there (RFC 2046 section 5.1.2), mime4j reads the line as text

#   MultipartWithoutDelimiter: a multipart has no boundary parameter, or none of its delimiters occurs; the module keeps it as one attachment of its declared type holding its body, mime4j as an empty multipart or as text

#   NonHeaderLineEndsSection: a header section holds a line with no field name before its empty line; the module ends the section there and that line starts the body (RFC 5322 section 3.6.8), mime4j reads later lines as fields or drops lines
#   UnpaddedFinalQuantum: a base64 part ends with two or three characters and no padding; the module decodes the octets they hold, mime4j drops them
